title: The Statute of Slapitations
logline: Barney discovers that the slap bet contract Marshall drafted in 2007 has a sunset clause: a thousand days without a slap and every remaining slap expires, at midnight tonight. Lily convenes the Slap Bet Commission, Ted signs on as Barney's lawyer, Robin runs the book, and Marshall spends twelve hours being outmaneuvered by the fine print he wrote himself.
coldOpen: Kids, in the fall of 2012, your Uncle Barney found a way out of the slap bet. He had twelve hours to survive. Uncle Marshall had twelve hours to slap him. And I, for reasons I still can't fully explain, was Barney's lawyer.

couch.line: Wait. This is a slap story?
Luke, it's a story about friendship.

scenes.summary: Twelve hours to midnight. Lily, in a 'robe' that is a cocktail dress, convenes the Slap Bet Commission from Barney's chair. Barney produces the 2007 contract: Article Nine expires all slaps after a thousand days without one. Flashback: Marshall wrote it himself. Barney has counted all 999 days, on a calendar with little hearts. Skulls. Ted is Barney's counsel, Robin runs the book, Marshall's watch is on Minnesota time. Lily rules the clause valid. Marshall goes for it; Article Four (no slaps during a hearing) stops him. Barney lawyers Marshall with his own word and leaves.

beats.line: Twelve hours before midnight, Uncle Barney summoned us to his office for what he called a formal proceeding.
This emergency session of the Slap Bet Commission will come to order.
Lily, that's my chair.
Not today. Today it's the bench.
Lily, that's a cocktail dress.
It's a robe if I say it's a robe. So ruled.
Barney, I have a deposition at one. Why does this need a commissioner?
Marshall. The original slap bet contract. Signed by all parties. Notarized by Carl.
Carl's not a notary.
He is for twenty dollars.
Article Nine. If one thousand days pass without a slap, all remaining slaps shall expire.
beats.title: The Slap Bet, Article Nine
lines: If one thousand days pass without a slap,

beats.line: That's insane. What idiot would put that in a slap bet?
You. In the booth. I was there.
Article Nine. If a thousand days ever pass without a slap, the slaps expire.
Baby, why would you put that in?
Every great contract has a sunset clause, Lily. It's elegant. It's how the big firms do it.
Also, Article Two has a comma splice.
Ted. A man is drafting.
Come on. Me, go a thousand days without slapping Barney? That's like a thousand days without a sandwich.
Your last slap was nine hundred and ninety-nine days ago.
Marshall. Why haven't you slapped him in almost three years?
I've been saving them, Lily! You don't open a fifty-year-old scotch on a Tuesday!
I do.
Wait. Nine hundred and ninety-nine? You've been counting?
Every single day. On a calendar. With a little heart.
Skull. A little skull.
At midnight, I'm a free man. Twelve hours. Tick tock.
It's eleven a.m. I have thirteen.
Your watch is still on Minnesota time?
Every watch I own is on Minnesota time. New York hasn't earned my hours.
Commissioner, I move to throw this whole thing out.
Objection. Ted Mosby, attorney for the slapee.
Ted, you're an architect!
I proofread the original. Fourteen commas. Four of them wrong. Nobody knows this document like me.
Dad. You're not a lawyer.
Penny, I studied law at Wesleyan. Well, audited. Well, I once held a door for a law professor.
And I'm running the book. Barney makes it to midnight, three to one.
Robin! You're supposed to be on my side!
I'm on the side that's holding everybody's money.
The Commission finds Article Nine valid. At midnight, all remaining slaps expire.
Lily! I'm your husband!
And the Commission is very sorry for your loss.
Fine. Then I'll use one right now.
Objection! Article Four. No slaps during an official hearing of the Commission.
Sustained.
I only wrote that so nobody would slap the judge!
And the judge thanks you, baby.
Then I move that this hearing stay in session until midnight.
Denied. The Commissioner has a pedicure. This hearing is adjourned.
Good luck, Marshall. Oh, and one more thing.
Lawyered.
He lawyered me. With my own contract. And my own word.
Line just moved. Five to one.

scenes.summary: Nine p.m. Barney circles Manhattan in the limo under Article Seven: no slaps in a moving vehicle. Lily rides along because the Commissioner must witness every slap, and Barney has a bar. Ranjit refuses to run red lights, so Marshall and Robin board at one. At the next light Ted argues the Earth is always moving, and Lily sustains it. Robin asks why Barney told Marshall at all; Barney says gloating. Ranjit pulls over at nine forty-four: he has twenty dollars on nine forty-five. Barney flees, Marshall chases, Ranjit misses by a minute.

beats.line: Nine p.m. Three hours left. Uncle Barney had found the one place in Manhattan he couldn't be slapped.
Article Seven. No slaps in a moving vehicle. Marshall wrote it after he watched a crash test video.
He cried for an hour. He said the dummies had families.
Ranjit, keep driving until midnight. Do not stop for anything.
Hello! What about red lights?
Especially red lights.
Mister Barney, I have never run a red light. Twenty years. It is the only thing my mother brags about.
And why is the Commissioner riding with me?
Article Five. The Commissioner must witness every slap. So I ride with whoever's more fun.
And you picked me.
You have a bar.
Red light!
Evening, Barney. Nice night for a drive.
Ranjit!
It was red.
And now it is green! We are moving!
Article Seven, Marshall. Sit back. Have a scotch. Watch your slaps die of old age.
Carl wants eleven fifty-eight. Twenty bucks. Done.
Red light!
We're stopped! Lily, the car is stopped!
Objection! The Earth spins at a thousand miles an hour. Nothing in New York is ever truly stopped.
Sustained. That was beautiful, Ted.
Lilypad!
In this limo, it's Commissioner.
I call you Lilypad in bed!
Not in my courtroom, you don't.
Barney, here's what's killing my odds. If you wanted them to expire, why tell him? You could've just kept quiet.
And miss the gloating? Robin, a win nobody sees is just a Tuesday.
Mister Barney, I am pulling over now.
Why? Is it gas? A flat? Is your mother okay?
No. Miss Robin has my twenty dollars on nine forty-five. It is nine forty-four.
Counsel. Legal advice.
Run.
Nine forty-six.

scenes.summary: Eleven-fifteen. Barney has vanished; Marshall ordered nachos. Robin's book is the biggest it's ever been: Barney has five hundred on himself, his own lawyer has five on him. Carl, the notary, keeps raising. Lily asks why Marshall really waited. Marshall's confession: he only had three slaps left, and every one he used made the slap bet shorter. Ted has college, Lily and Robin have 'sandwiches', he and Barney have a contract. Lily: it's a friendship, not a gift card. His Minnesota watch says he has an hour and forty-five minutes. Robin plays hockey: Article Eight, no slaps near a ledge. He's on the roof. Robin insists they walk there slowly.

beats.line: By eleven-fifteen, Barney had vanished, and Uncle Marshall did what he always does in a crisis. He ordered nachos.
Biggest book I've ever run. Barney bet five hundred on himself. His own lawyer bet five.
beats.title: Robin's Book: The Slap

beats.line: Robin, can I move my bet to eleven forty-five? I have a really good feeling.
Line's closed, Wendy.
Doubling eleven fifty-eight.
Carl, you notarized the contract. That's a conflict of interest.
Tripling.
Marshall. Commissioner to husband. Why did you really wait nine hundred and ninety-nine days?
Because there were only three left, Lily. Every one I used, the slap bet got shorter.
Ted and I have college. You and Robin have whatever you two do on the roof at two in the morning.
Sandwiches.
Barney and I have a contract. When it runs out, what are we? Two guys who used to slap?
Baby. It's a friendship. Not a gift card.
A gift card that expires at midnight, Lily!
Okay. Okay. By my watch, I still have an hour and forty-five minutes.
Marshall. Your watch is in Minnesota.
So is my heart, Robin!
Hockey rule. You don't chase the puck. You go where it's going. What other hiding spots are in that contract?
Hearings. Moving vehicles. And Article Eight. No slaps within ten feet of a ledge.
Why a ledge?
Safety, Lily! Someone could get slapped right off a building!
He's on the roof.
Then let's go get my slap.
Great. Let's walk. Slowly. Very, very slowly.

scenes.summary: Eleven fifty-two. Barney sits on the parapet with Ted under Article Eight. Ted's pedantry (it's a parapet) costs him fines. Marshall's water-tower lure fails. Marshall tells Barney why he waited, and lets the slaps go. Robin begs him to slap at 11:59; he won't. Midnight. Barney steps off the ledge and admits he told Marshall because Marshall is the only person who ever promised, in writing, to come back for him. The calendar had hearts. Skulls. Ted reads Article One: all deadlines run on the drafter's wristwatch. It's 11:01. Barney: legen... Robin: wait for it, she has 11:59. Fifty-eight silent minutes later, the slap. Dary. See you in nine hundred and ninety-nine days.

beats.line: Eight minutes, counsel. Start drafting my victory speech.
Already done. It's mostly about punctuation.
Sorry we're late. I made us take the stairs. Twice.
Barney. Step away from the ledge.
Article Eight, Marshall. Ten feet. You beautiful, safety-conscious man.
Ted. Is that technically a ledge?
No. It's a parapet.
Lily! It's a parapet! Not a ledge!
Overruled. A parapet is a ledge. Ted, that's a five dollar fine for saying parapet.
It's the correct word!
Ten.
Barney, look. There's a gorgeous woman by the water tower.
Marshall, I've been on this roof for two hours. I would know.
You want to know why I waited nine hundred and ninety-nine days? I was scared of running out.
But I don't need a contract to be your friend. Keep them, Barney. I'm letting them go.
No! It's eleven fifty-nine! Slap him! Slap him now!
Three. Two. One.
Midnight. The slaps have expired.
I could have kept my mouth shut, you know. Let midnight sneak by. You never would have noticed.
So why didn't you?
My whole life, people said they'd come back for me. My dad. Every woman I ever met.
Okay, that one's on me.
You're the only guy who ever promised, in writing, that he'd always come back. Even if it was to hit me in the face.
That's why the calendar had little hearts.
Skulls, Marshall. They were skulls.
Actually.
Ted!
No, you'll want this one. Article One. Nobody ever reads Article One. It's definitions.
All deadlines run on the official clock of the slap bet. Defined as the drafter's wristwatch.
My watch says eleven-oh-one.
I may have just lost my first case.
Well, Marshall. Fifty-nine minutes. Make it legen—
Wait for it!
That's my line.
Eleven fifty-nine, contract time. I have two hundred dollars on it.
The Commission will allow it.
Fifty-eight minutes of total silence later. After nine hundred and ninety-nine days, Uncle Barney could wait for it.
Dary.
Eleven fifty-nine. The house always wins.
See you in a thousand days, buddy.
Nine hundred and ninety-nine.
Kids, every nine hundred and ninety-nine days, Uncle Barney still calls Uncle Marshall to gloat. Then he goes and waits somewhere easy to find.
